headline: All majors above the 200-day line with RSI in the 80s, but whale flows reversed hard onto exchanges this week.
paragraphs: The regime is long. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all trade above their 200-day simple moving average, with MACD above signal across the board. Dogecoin and Cardano are the outliers, sitting below the 200-day line despite positive momentum. No golden crosses have formed yet, which means the recovery is not a structural trend reversal but rather a strong relief move within a downtrend: these assets remain deeply underwater on the year. Bitcoin is 37.9% below its 12-month high of $124,740; Ethereum trails by 49.4%; Solana is down 62.9%; Cardano has lost 76.5%. The crowd has bought back hard into this rally, pushing fear-greed to 72 (Greed territory), and the 30-day range spans from 25 to 72, showing the sentiment has swung from deep fear to near-euphoria in a month.

Momentum is overbought and disconnected from conviction. Every major asset carries an RSI-14 above 80, with Ethereum at 86.9 and Bitcoin at 85.5. MACD is positive across the board, but overbought momentum without golden crosses means the rally is running on inertia, not structural buying. This is a classic setup for a pullback, though the tape does not say when or by how much. The outliers are telling: Dogecoin has a long/short ratio of 3.44 on perpetuals, meaning leveraged longs are crowded three-to-one against shorts. SOL shows 1.77 longs per short. When positioning gets that skewed to one side, any reversal can trigger cascade liquidations. The data shows exactly that risk in the open interest: SOL shorts were liquidated for $9 million in the last 24 hours, while ETH longs got blown out for $4 million. XRP saw $5.4 million in long liquidations versus $4 million in shorts, suggesting buyers were testing the highs. Funding rates are flat across all venues at 0.01% per 8-hour period, annualizing to 11%, which is moderate and not a screaming panic-sell signal.

Derivatives positioning reveals a market that wants higher but may not have the money to keep pushing. Bitcoin open interest at OKX sits at $2.3 billion with a 1.11 long/short ratio; Ethereum at $1.43 billion with 1.13 longs per short. Those are not extreme crowding numbers, but they are leaning bullish. The real tension shows up in altcoin positioning: Dogecoin at 3.44 long/short and SOL at 1.77 suggest retail and retail-adjacent leverage is heavily concentrated in meme and high-beta assets. When those positions blow, they may not reverse the majors, but they will pull liquidity from the tape and force spot selling to cover margin.

Whale flows flipped from accumulation to distribution this week, and it is not subtle. Over the last five sessions through August 21, $392.6 million moved onto exchanges in net terms, composed of $230.9 million in Bitcoin and $161.6 million in Ethereum. The weekly breakdown is stark: weeks ending July 31 and August 7 saw $1.06 billion and $316 million move off exchanges (accumulation, cold storage moves, or long-term holder buybacks). Weeks ending August 14 and August 21 saw $405 million and then $553 million move back onto exchanges. The stablecoin float sits at $307.7 billion, down 0.12% over 30 days, so dry powder is not building; it is flat. The biggest whale moves in the last 24 hours show $1.1 billion in USDT flowing onto Binance and Bitfinex, while $900 million in USDT and $180 million in USDC moved off from Binance and Coinbase Institutional. The net effect is ambiguous: large stablecoin inflows could be preparing for a dip buy, or they could be a distribution by whales before they move spot out. The fact that Bitcoin and Ethereum spot also moved onto exchanges at the same time skews the read toward the latter. Bitcoin ETF flows on August 20 printed a $606 million inflow, with the last five sessions showing $1.55 billion in net inflows and four same-direction days. Ethereum saw $219.5 million on the latest date and $508.6 million over five sessions, also four same-direction days. Traditional finance is bidding, but spot whales are selling into it.

Sentiment has climbed to Greed at 72, but the tape underneath shows hesitation and rotation. The 24-hour movers are broad and meme-heavy: Dogecoin up 7.83%, ADA up 9.94%, XRP up 8.13%. These are the trades the crowd piles into when it feels safe. At the same time, the majors show extreme RSI readings, whale flows are reversing, and altcoin leverage is lopsided. Bitcoin dominance stands at 59.2%, which is not extreme but reflects the flight to safety from the micro-caps. Network fees on Bitcoin are low (6 satoshis per byte fastest, 4 for next-hour confirmation), and the difficulty is ticking down 1.3% ahead of retarget, signals of easing pressure rather than capitulation.

Watch for three conditions. First, whether the whale flow reversal persists into next week or whether the on-exchange deposits prove to be capitulation buys disguised as distribution. Second, a break of the 200-day line by any major, especially Bitcoin, which would signal the relief is exhausted. Third, a move below 70 on the fear-greed index or a 5% single-day drawdown on Bitcoin, either of which would test whether the leveraged altcoin longs hold or flush out. The tape as it stands shows a crowd in euphoria, whales exiting into bid, and momentum divorced from trend. That combination has not usually persisted for long.
